## Answer
The late-delivery rate increased from 2.91% to 4.39% in 2017-09, which could be due to a combination of factors including changes in delivery performance, order volume, or seller behavior. The increase in average delivery time and decrease in average promised delivery window suggest potential issues with delivery efficiency or expectations.

## Findings
- Late-delivery rate increased by 1.48 percentage points (from 2.91% to 4.39%).
- Average delivery time increased by 0.7 days (from 11.0 to 11.7 days).
- Average promised delivery window decreased by 1.0 day (from 24.1 to 23.1 days).
- Orders decreased by 46 (from 4331 to 4285).
- Average order value increased by 14.14 R$ (from 155.65 to 169.79 R$).
- Low-review rate increased by 1.07 percentage points (from 11.35% to 12.42%).
- Cancellation rate remained stable at 1.36% to 1.35%.

## Investigate first
- Analyze the performance of sellers with the highest late-delivery rates in 2017-09 to identify any patterns or commonalities.
- Examine the distribution of late deliveries by region to determine if certain areas experienced more delays.
- Investigate the impact of the increased average order value on delivery performance and whether it correlates with any changes in product categories.

## Limitations
- The data does not provide granular details on specific sellers, regions, or product categories.
- There is no information on the reasons for late deliveries or the specific products involved.
- The data does not include customer feedback or reviews for the late deliveries.
